Direct laryngobronchoscopy was done and showed multiple nodules on both vocal cords with significant narrowing and edema of the larynx, as shown in Figure 3. He was later referred to our chest clinic for further evaluation. Based on the clinical presentation and lack of response to the given therapy, Farber disease was highly suspected and was later confirmed genetically by genetic testing that revealed a homozygous mutation in the ASAH1 gene (p.Gly213Glu (GGA > GAA): c.638G > A in exon 8).
